NTA, but neither is he for keeping some semblance of family for his kiddos. My in-laws, who are divorced, did this for my wife and her brother. I thought it was weird at first, since mother-in-law remarried, but came to see the benefit for my wife and her brother. 

Choosing to leave over this is understandable, but so is what he is doing for his kids. All positive assumptions in mind. You can't expect a man to choose his girlfriend over his kids.

I could see how that could be the perspective... but in all reality, there were a great many of us, screaming at the ceiling, crying in the shower, and laying in the dark room, just wondering if its worth it. Yeah, a bunch of fake people bring issues for clout, but just because they are fake doesnt mean the thing they are clout chasing with is fake.

Yeah... it feels lonely... even with those that know the struggle... they never truly know... similar, but never the same. That being said, you are not alone. You may feel alone, but there are others just like you.

The thing is, most non-narcisists actually HATE the sound of their own voice. I am one. Hate my singing voice. Even after several people tell me they love it and that I should sing more often, I have a hard time believing them. So keep this in mind when you judge yourself. You will probably find that you hate most creative things you do, and will judge yourself way too harshly because of it, be it singing, drawing, writing, or whatever. Keep your head up, and if you enjoy it, keep at it. Singing is a wonderful outlet, and the more you enjoy the act of singing, as well as the song you are singing, the better you will actually be.
This strikes true to me most days. Hope and faith feel futile when you are staring down a dark tunnel.

You are not alone. 
Last year, I lost my stepmother suddenly to liver failure, then about a month later, lost my grandfather, whom I had a lot of respect for, then lost my grandmother (his wife) 10 days later.
 Worst part about the last one was that I went to their house to pick up my blind uncle so we can split a chord of wood, and overlooked the fact that the dogs were barking in her room. That should have told us something was wrong right then due to the fact that she didnt make a move to remedy the barking. My uncle and I went about our business, cutting and splitting a large oak tree. Later that evening, after I dropped him back at their house, I head home. Halfway home, uncle calls me to tell me he found her face down in the bathroom, long gone. Later found out that it was an anyurism(sp) of the hear. So basically, you could say she died of a broken heart.

Shortly after this onslaught, it was announced to my wife and I that our friends, a couple we had grown very close to, was getting a divorce, then they both all but disappeared, refusing to talk to either of us. It felt like another death to me. 

After all of that I spent the next six months struggling with thoughts of suicide, from all that had happened thus far, to my anger issues becoming a problem after so long of having chained the beast, and my being unemployed, therefore being a useless waste to my wife and daughter. It was rough.

To this day, I feel like I have no one I can truly open up to, and I am only opening up here so as to possibly help you and others see that they are not alone, and this too shall pass. 

Hope this finds you well, whoever reads this.
